scope: Bounded HAOS-IIP recoverability predictions. These are diagnostic records, not proofs of new physics or biology.

prediction_levels.P0_toy_internal: Supported only by toy or in-repo demonstrations.
prediction_levels.P1_cross_system: Supported across more than one toy or internal system.
prediction_levels.P2_external_dataset: Ready for external data or third-party benchmark tests.
prediction_levels.P3_field_facing: A field-facing diagnostic prediction with clear controls.
prediction_levels.P4_physics_candidate: A candidate physics-facing prediction requiring external replication.

records.title: Recoverability loss precedes visible failure under controlled perturbation
records.prediction_statement: In bounded interacting systems, a sustained recoverability collapse index should appear before visible or conventional failure under controlled monotone perturbation.
records.novelty_boundary: This is a field-facing diagnostic candidate: it predicts an ordering between recoverability loss and visible failure, not a new substrate or new physical law.
records.perturbation: A deterministic monotone perturbation sweep from intact baseline to maximum stress.
pass_criteria: baseline recoverability is high
recoverability declines under perturbation
k_star is defined before first visible_failure
result is deterministic across repeated runs
fail_criteria: visible_failure appears before k_star
recoverability is flat or non-informative under perturbation
the result changes across deterministic reruns
falsifiers: If matched systems repeatedly show visible failure before recoverability collapse under the stated perturbation protocol, this prediction fails for that system class.
records.next_external_test: Apply the same ordering test to an external time-series network dataset with known failure or degradation labels.
limitations: Current support is from deterministic toy systems.
External systems may require different visible failure markers.
non_claims: Does not claim HAOS-IIP proves biology.
Does not claim new physics.
Does not replace domain-specific models.

records.title: Collapse-origin localization precedes global failure
records.prediction_statement: The earliest localized recoverability break should identify the sector, branch, or patch where later visible failure concentrates.
records.novelty_boundary: This predicts a diagnostic localization rule, not a new mechanism of failure.
records.perturbation: Localized or structured perturbation applied to a known branch, patch, or sector.
pass_criteria: the earliest local recoverability collapse occurs before global visible failure
the same local sector overlaps the later visible failure region
matched controls do not show the same localization by chance
fail_criteria: local recoverability collapse is spatially uncorrelated with later visible failure
global failure occurs without any prior local recoverability signal
the localization signal disappears under deterministic robustness variations
falsifiers: If local k_origin repeatedly fails to overlap later failure regions better than matched controls, this prediction fails for that system class.

current_evidence.result: fragile branch was designed to degrade earlier than whole-network failure

records.next_external_test: Add local-sector readouts to Lines B-D, then test on external degradation maps where failure regions are labeled.
limitations: Current evidence is design-level and internal.
Requires spatial or sector labels to test fairly.
non_claims: Does not claim universal localization.
Does not claim causal proof from correlation.
Does not replace mechanistic failure analysis.

records.title: Safety margin decays before conventional threshold failure
records.prediction_statement: A safety_margin derived from recoverability collapse should approach zero before conventional visible failure thresholds are crossed.
records.novelty_boundary: This predicts a pre-failure margin observable. It does not claim that safety_margin is a conserved physical quantity.
system_scope: general weighted interaction graphs under monotone stress
records.perturbation: Controlled perturbation sweep with a defined collapse threshold and visible failure threshold.
pass_criteria: safety_margin is positive before k_star
safety_margin reaches zero at k_star
visible_failure occurs after safety_margin reaches zero
fail_criteria: visible_failure occurs while safety_margin is still positive
safety_margin oscillates without useful warning
k_star cannot be stably identified
falsifiers: If visible failure consistently occurs before safety_margin reaches zero under the defined protocol, this prediction fails for that system class.

current_evidence.result: Lines A-D all record k_star before first visible failure.

records.next_external_test: Fit safety_margin on one perturbation family and test whether it forecasts visible failure on a held-out perturbation family.
limitations: Threshold choice affects k_star and safety_margin.
External calibration is required before operational use.
non_claims: Does not claim risk can be predicted without controls.
Does not claim a universal numerical threshold.
Does not replace existing safety analysis.

records.title: Recoverability gradients expose hidden fragile branches
records.prediction_statement: In coupled systems with a weak downstream branch, recoverability gradients should reveal branch degradation before whole-system function appears visibly impaired.
records.novelty_boundary: This is a diagnostic hypothesis about hidden fragility, not a claim that HAOS-IIP discovers biological or physical mechanisms by itself.
system_scope: interaction graphs with hub and branch motifs
records.perturbation: Progressive weakening of edges feeding a known fragile branch or weakly supported sector.
pass_criteria: branch_recoverability declines before whole-system visible failure
recoverability_gradient identifies the fragile branch before global collapse
matched non-fragile branches remain more stable under the same perturbation
fail_criteria: branch and whole-system recoverability decline at the same time
recoverability_gradient does not distinguish fragile from non-fragile branches
visible failure appears with no prior branch-level warning
falsifiers: If branch recoverability gives no earlier signal than whole-system readouts across matched fragile-branch systems, this prediction fails.

current_evidence.result: fragile downstream branch shows earlier degradation than the whole network in the Line A validation logic

records.next_external_test: Use a real or benchmark directed network with known vulnerable branches and compare branch recoverability against standard centrality or degree metrics.
limitations: Requires branch definitions or sector extraction.
Toy evidence is not field validation.
non_claims: Does not claim hidden branches exist in every system.
Does not claim causal mechanism without intervention.
Does not replace domain-specific fragility metrics.

records.title: Shell-native observables can close while raw local gradients remain open
records.prediction_statement: For some kernel-graph systems, shell-native recoverability observables should show stable closure under perturbation while raw local-gradient observables remain residual or open.
records.novelty_boundary: This is a physics-adjacent observable-frame prediction. It does not assert that the graph is physical spacetime or that closure proves a continuum law.
system_scope: discrete interaction graphs with shell or radial organization
external graph datasets where shell-like grouping can be independently defined
records.perturbation: Matched disorder, localized bump, or smooth inhomogeneity perturbations applied to graph observables.
pass_criteria: shell-native closure remains stable under defined perturbation
raw local-gradient readout remains open or residual under the same protocol
matched controls do not erase the split
fail_criteria: raw local-gradient and shell-native observables behave identically under controls
shell-native closure disappears under deterministic robustness checks
the split depends on post-hoc threshold tuning
falsifiers: If independently grouped shell-native observables fail to separate from raw local-gradient residuals under matched controls, this prediction fails for that graph class.

current_evidence.result: internal bridge separates shell-native closures from raw local-gradient open boundaries

records.next_external_test: Apply the same shell-native versus raw-gradient split to an independently generated graph family with pre-registered grouping rules.
limitations: Current evidence is internal to HAOS-IIP graph families.
Shell grouping must be pre-registered to avoid post-hoc closure.
non_claims: Does not claim a continuum limit.
Does not claim physical spacetime emergence.
Does not claim new physics without external replication.

records.title: Polar-mode address selection in layered ferroelectrics
records.prediction_statement: In layered polar ferroelectrics or closely related polar oxyhalides, pulsed excitation should produce a narrowband coherent readout concentrated in a pre-registered target window around an independently measured polar transverse optical mode, while non-polar or mode-mismatched controls should not show the same target-window recoverability.
records.novelty_boundary: This is a field-facing diagnostic prediction seeded by the ferron sidecar. It predicts a recoverability signature around independently measured polar modes, not a universal harmonic grid or a new materials theory.
system_scope: matched non-polar or mode-mismatched control materials
records.perturbation: Pulsed optical excitation with pre-registered target-frequency windows derived from independent polar phonon measurements.
pass_criteria: target-window peak is found in at least 80 percent of controlled polar-material records
linewidth proxy is below 0.1 THz when spectra support linewidth estimation
mean spectral recoverability is at least 0.85
non-polar or mode-mismatched controls fail at least one target-window recoverability criterion
fail_criteria: matched polar materials repeatedly show only broadband emission under the stated excitation protocol
the dominant peak misses the pre-registered polar-mode target window
non-polar or mode-mismatched controls show the same target-window recoverability as the polar material
falsifiers: If matched polar materials repeatedly show only broadband emission, or if non-polar controls show the same target-window recoverability under matched excitation, this prediction fails for that material class.

current_evidence.result: 15/15 target-window peaks near 3.13 THz; mean_peak_frequency_THz=3.13893; mean_spectral_recoverability=0.928455

current_evidence.source: papers/pdf_releases/64.1 Materials Bridge Line A - Ferron Coherence Recoverability Probe for HAOS-IIP.pdf
current_evidence.result: External-data bridge status PASS; raw STFT-grid boundary preserved

records.next_external_test: Run a pre-registered pump-probe or THz emission scan on a matched polar versus non-polar material set using independently measured polar-mode target windows.
limitations: Thresholds are provisional and seeded by one ferron sidecar.
Independent polar phonon measurements are required before target-window selection.
Control-material matching must be specified before data inspection.
non_claims: Does not claim ferrons prove HAOS-IIP.
Does not claim a universal harmonic grid.
Does not replace material-specific lattice dynamics.

records.title: Thickness and boundary dependence of target-band propagation
records.prediction_statement: In NbOI2-like or WO2Br2-like flakes, target-band packet arrival time should increase with pump-probe separation, and the group-velocity proxy should change with thickness or confinement under matched excitation.
records.novelty_boundary: This is a propagation-readout prediction for bounded target-band envelopes. It does not claim that the published target-band traces are raw STFT maps.
system_scope: NbOI2-like polar flakes with controlled thickness
WO2Br2-like polar flakes with controlled thickness
matched geometry controls without polar propagation
records.perturbation: Controlled pump-probe separation and thickness or confinement sweep under matched excitation conditions.
pass_criteria: peak time versus distance fit has positive slope
monotonic peak-delay fraction is at least 0.75
group velocity differs between at least two controlled thickness groups by more than experimental uncertainty
target-band recoverability remains above 0.70 before visible propagation failure
fail_criteria: distance-ordered peak delay is absent while the target-band signal remains measurable
group velocity does not vary with thickness or confinement beyond experimental uncertainty
matched geometry controls reproduce the same propagation-readout pattern
falsifiers: If controlled thickness series show no distance-ordered peak delay and no thickness dependence beyond uncertainty while the target-band signal remains measurable, this prediction fails for that material class.

current_evidence.result: 8 published target-band traces; 216 time points; group velocity proxies 58.8 km/s at 96 nm and 100 km/s at 224 nm; monotonic_peak_delay=1.0 in both groups

records.next_external_test: Acquire a controlled-thickness distance series and pre-register the slope, monotonicity, and velocity-consistency criteria before target-band envelope extraction.
limitations: Published Fig. 2d traces are post-processed target-band envelopes, not raw time-frequency grids.
Thickness labels in raw Fig. 2a/Fig. 2b traces require assignment against published trace ordering.
Velocity thresholds must account for sample preparation and measurement uncertainty.
non_claims: Does not claim universal velocity values.
Does not claim raw STFT-grid validation.
Does not replace material-specific propagation modeling.

records.title: Target-window re-addressing after secondary perturbation
records.prediction_statement: After a secondary pulse, controlled defect scattering, or mild boundary perturbation below damage threshold, the coherent readout should preferentially return to the original target frequency window before the full amplitude envelope necessarily recovers.
records.novelty_boundary: This predicts a recoverability ordering for a pre-registered target frequency. It does not claim that the material has memory in a cognitive or ontological sense.
system_scope: NbOI2-like polar flakes under multi-pulse excitation
WO2Br2-like polar flakes under multi-pulse excitation
polar materials with controlled defect or boundary scattering below damage threshold
records.perturbation: A secondary pulse, mild defect scattering, or boundary perturbation applied below irreversible damage threshold after the initial coherent target-band response is established.
pass_criteria: post-perturbation peak frequency returns to the pre-registered target window
frequency stability is at least 0.95
mean target-window spectral recoverability is at least 0.85
broadband background does not dominate the recovered target-window signal
fail_criteria: secondary perturbation repeatedly produces broadband thermalization with no target-window recovery
a different dominant frequency replaces the original target window under matched non-damaging perturbation
target-window recoverability cannot be distinguished from broadband background
falsifiers: If secondary perturbation repeatedly produces broadband thermalization or a different dominant frequency with no preferential recovery of the original target window, this prediction fails for that perturbation regime.

current_evidence.result: mean spectral recoverability 0.928455 and no sustained k_star under current thresholds

records.next_external_test: Run multi-pulse target-band recovery experiments with pre-registered delay windows and damage controls.
limitations: No secondary-pulse external dataset has been tested in this repo yet.
Damage threshold and heating controls must be specified before interpreting non-recovery.
Amplitude recovery and frequency recovery may decouple.
non_claims: Does not claim a universal echo effect.
Does not claim quantum consciousness or memory.
Does not claim recovery outside non-damaging perturbation regimes.

records.title: Target-window recoverability separates coherent propagation records from broadband controls
records.prediction_statement: Across external datasets with pre-registered narrowband collective modes, HAOS-style target-window recoverability should separate coherent directional propagation records from broadband or non-propagating controls better than amplitude-only ranking.
records.novelty_boundary: This is a cross-dataset diagnostic prediction. It does not assert that unrelated material systems share a literal HAOS-IIP substrate.
system_scope: published narrowband collective-mode datasets with time or distance readouts
directional propagation records with pre-registered target windows
records.perturbation: Dataset-level comparison across pre-registered coherent propagation records and matched broadband or non-propagating controls.
pass_criteria: target-window recoverability separates coherent propagation records from controls in a held-out dataset
the separation survives fixed thresholds chosen before inspection
amplitude-only ranking performs worse or is less stable under matched controls
fail_criteria: target-window recoverability does not outperform amplitude-only ranking
fixed thresholds fail to distinguish coherent propagation records from controls
the separation disappears when target windows are pre-registered rather than chosen post hoc
falsifiers: If pre-registered target-window recoverability does not distinguish coherent propagation records from broadband or non-propagating controls better than amplitude-only baselines, this prediction fails for the selected dataset class.

current_evidence.result: ferron_persistence_proxy=0.957192 from spectral, published propagation, and computed diagnostic components

records.next_external_test: Pre-register a small literature or public-data benchmark with narrowband propagation records and matched broadband controls, then compare target-window recoverability against amplitude-only ranking.
limitations: This record is broader than the ferron dataset and therefore remains P2 until a cross-dataset benchmark is run.
Target windows must be chosen from independent measurements or paper-declared modes before scoring.
Dataset curation can bias separation if controls are not matched.
non_claims: Does not claim cross-material universality.
Does not claim a literal shared substrate.
Does not replace field-specific coherence metrics.
